gen-gf-domine-gf-cascadia-code: Bookish bulbs and wire-thin lines. Cascadia Code spaces its sans letters far apart, so a bigger body size gives them room while Domine keeps its sturdy hairlines up top.
gen-gf-domine-gf-cascadia-mono: Domine leans literary, with bowls like blown glass bulbs. It handles authority through gently thickened curves, while Cascadia Mono does its work as a plain sans of bent-pipe strokes, compact and uniform.
gen-gf-domine-gf-julius-sans-one: Gently thickening shoulders give Domine a literary, glassy pace. Julius Sans One then lays a single-weight outline across the page, its sans letters spread wide with hardly any gap between capital and lowercase height.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-exa: Authoritative, a little bookish. A long run of Lexend Exa sans text would feel brisk and wide, big x-height and untapered strokes carrying you along after Domine's modestly tapered joins.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-giga: Domine's curves thicken gently, a middle path between monoline and razor-thin. Lexend Giga sits beneath as sans text with flat, single-weight strokes and generous tracking, so the two feel clearly different yet agreeable.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-mega: Mild thick-thin shifts smooth Domine's reading pace. Lexend Mega, a sans-serif cut from one gauge of tubing, gives the page a plainer, friendlier voice, with its c shapes gaping visibly.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-peta: Lexend Peta brings dowel-straight stems and wide-mouthed curves, with a big x-height. And Domine, its curves carrying a reed pen's slight thickening, makes this sans-serif partner feel all the more uniform.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera reads like a plotter pen at work, single-weight and spaced like stepping stones. And if Domine's shaded texture were shrunk small, that subtle swell would fade, whereas a sans this wide holds up large.
gen-gf-domine-gf-lexend-zetta: Approachable, first of all, with Domine's slight swell on its bowls. Lexend Zetta, a plain sans of ribbon-like constant strokes and wide tracking, skims along through a long stretch with real ease.
gen-gf-domine-gf-montserrat-alternates: Literary swagger meets chalk-board lowercase. Domine shows faint nib pressure across its rounds, and Montserrat Alternates, a sans-serif with zero modulation, does the opposite and keeps its line crisp.
